editorNote: A mixed day: cryptography archaeology, a vendor's own benchmark gains, two looks at how AI is measured and used at work, and the hardware to run big models at home. Figures come from the linked primary pages, and vendor claims are marked as such.

stories.headline: Anthropic says a research model traced the NIST elliptic-curve seeds to lrand48 and Unix timestamps
stories.summary: Anthropic reports an internal research model worked out, in under half an hour, how the standardised P-192 through P-521 seeds were generated: not as hash outputs but from the C library's lrand48 seeded with timestamps dated between May 1997 and April 1998. Several base points and the B-163 seed remain unexplained.
stories.whyItMatters: Anthropic says this is not a cryptographic break, and that a simple, reproducible generation process makes a backdoor much less plausible.

sourceLinks.title: Anthropic: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins

stories.headline: DeepSeek ships V4.1 Flash 1017, an MIT-licensed 763B-parameter update with a 1M-token context
stories.summary: The new checkpoint is billed as a minor update aimed at reasoning, coding and agentic tasks, with shorter outputs. By DeepSeek's own numbers, Terminal-Bench 4.0 rises from 31.2 to 42.3 and HLE without tools from 36.8 to 42.6.
stories.whyItMatters: Weights are MIT-licensed; the benchmark figures are the vendor's own, and the page shows Opus 5 ahead on most other listed benchmarks.

stories.headline: Claude Code team: stop reading every line, minimise human review time without raising reverts
stories.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code team says Claude writes about 90% of its code, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September while the revert share fell by more than 40%. Review is layered: automated agents, security review, CI, then risk-tiered human approval.
stories.whyItMatters: It is Anthropic describing its own team's results, but the post gives concrete figures, including internal PRs needing five or more review rounds falling from 8.9% to 1.5%.

sourceLinks.title: How the Claude Code team does code review

stories.headline: Mercor estimates about 90% of US working hours go to tasks AI benchmarks barely cover
stories.summary: Mercor mapped 29 benchmarks onto 923 O*NET occupations and 18,797 tasks. It estimates about 90% of US working hours fall on tasks with little or no benchmark coverage, and six job families have no well-covered occupation.
stories.whyItMatters: The authors call results provisional and say an incomplete benchmark list likely biases coverage downward.

sourceLinks.title: Mercor: A benchmark map of the US economy

stories.headline: Apple benchmarks 816B Muse Spark Open across four M5 Ultra Mac Studios linked by Thunderbolt 5
stories.summary: Apple's MLX team reports 36.73 tokens/s decode at 8,192 context on four M5 Ultra machines using tensor parallelism over RDMA, for a model needing about 493GB in NVFP4. A single M5 Ultra has up to 4.6x faster time to first token than an M3 Ultra.
stories.whyItMatters: The numbers show what a local setup of this size can do; two-machine tensor parallelism was slower than pipeline for long-context prefill.

sourceLinks.title: Apple ML Research: MLX distributed inference

stories.headline: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6B image model that runs in 8GB of VRAM
stories.summary: The model handles text-to-image, editing and up to 10 reference images, with native 4K and bounding-box control. BFL says the distilled INT8 build makes a 1MP image in about 4 seconds on an RTX 5090.
stories.whyItMatters: Free commercial use is limited to those under $5M annual revenue; larger organisations need self-hosted licensing or the API.

sourceLinks.title: Black Forest Labs: FLUX 3 Image Klein
